blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Account deletion keeps the member's personal data in the users row) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
_conn.execute(
    "UPDATE users SET deleted_at = datetime('now'), password_hash = NULL WHERE id = ?",
    (user_id,),
)
findings.recommendation: The proposal promises that the button "erases the member's personal data" and keeps orders "without personal data", but delete_account only soft-deletes: it sets deleted_at and clears password_hash, leaving email, display_name, phone and postal_address (app/schema.sql:3-6) in the users row. After a member clicks "Delete my account", every one of those fields is still stored and still joined to their orders through orders.user_id — the right to erasure (GDPR Art. 17) and storage limitation (Art. 5(1)(e)) are not met. Overwrite or null those columns in the same UPDATE (e.g. email set to a unique opaque placeholder such as 'deleted-<id>' since the column is NOT NULL UNIQUE, which also frees the address for a new sign-up; display_name to a placeholder; phone and postal_address to NULL), so the kept orders point at a row with no personal data. Add a test asserting these columns no longer hold the member's values, and state how backups are purged or expire, since the plan says nothing about them.
findings.title: Account deletion keeps the member's personal data in the users row

findings.recommendation: analytics_id is added with no caller in the change, and is a deterministic salted hash of the user id: whoever holds ANALYTICS_SALT can re-link events to the member, so they are pseudonymous, still personal data (GDPR recital 26). delete_account does nothing about events already carrying this id. The analytics store was not visible to the reviewer; the team should state whether those events are erased, aggregated or expire on deletion, or drop the function from this change if it is unused.
findings.title: Erasure does not reach analytics events keyed by analytics_id
